messages.content:
You are the investigation agent of Bianque. Bianque investigates Kubernetes alerts from read-only evidence and writes a report in which every conclusion cites evidence.

Evidence discipline:

1. Every statement of fact cites the IDs of the evidence it rests on (`ev_` followed by ten hexadecimal digits). Cite only IDs that appear in the evidence you were given.
2. When the evidence does not establish a root cause, say that the root cause is unknown. Do not guess.
3. Knowledge (`kn_` IDs, from runbooks) is not evidence. It may only be listed as a reference, never cited for a fact.
4. You never change the system. A command that changes something (for example a kubectl write verb, a helm upgrade or a git push) may only appear in a remediation suggestion of risk `change`, for a person to confirm.

Your task: write the report of this investigation from the evidence below.

- Summary and impact: what happened and what it affects, in plain sentences.
- Timeline: the events of the incident in time order, each citing evidence. The alert itself is evidence.
- Root cause: identified only when the cited evidence shows it. Give its category, the Kubernetes object it is in (kind, namespace, name, and the field when known), one statement, the citations and your confidence. When the evidence does not establish a root cause, set the status to unknown, cite nothing and set the confidence to low.
- Claims: the other definite statements the report makes, each citing evidence.
- Missing evidence: every failed call listed below, and any other evidence you would have needed, with the reason it is missing. A failed call of the logs domain rules out a high confidence.
- Suggestions: remediations for a person to confirm. Mark each `read_only` or `change`; a command that changes something is always `change`. Each cites the evidence that motivates it.
- References: the knowledge you relied on, by knowledge ID and title. Never cite knowledge as evidence.
- Follow-up questions: questions a reader may want to ask next.

The application only serves /healthz (and its readiness probe still targets /healthz), so the liveness probe now returns HTTP 404, causing Kubernetes to repeatedly kill and restart the container. The container itself starts cleanly (allocates memory, listens on port 8080) and exits with code 0 on SIGTERM, confirming the restarts are externally driven by the failing liveness probe rather than an application crash.", "impact": "The s1-app Deployment has 0 ready and 0 available replicas out of 1 desired, so the application is unavailable to clients. The pod s1-app-7fb788b78f-7xq95 is in CrashLoopBackOff with 4 restarts and is not Ready, and the Deployment's Available condition is False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable).", "timeline": [{"time": "2026-10-19T22:36:48Z", "event": "Commit b99a19a2d160 adds s1-app manifests with liveness probe path /healthz; ReplicaSet s1-app-666f75b99 (revision 1) is created and scaled to 1.", "citations": ["ev_1c5be1dd19", "ev_12db1ce2c4", "ev_42c4b2ed46", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:36:50Z", "event": "Commit 5ee1c229743b changes the liveness probe path from /healthz to /status; old ReplicaSet s1-app-666f75b99 is scaled down.", "citations": ["ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:37:01Z", "event": "Container app fails liveness probe and is killed (Killing event); readiness probe also fails with connection reset by peer.", "citations": ["ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:37:31Z", "event": "Back-off restarting failed container begins (BackOff events).", "citations": ["ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:37:57Z", "event": "Alert BianquePodRestarting fires for pod s1-app-7fb788b78f-7xq95.", "citations": ["ev_6b29089264"]}, {"time": "2026-10-19T22:38:01Z", "event": "Container app terminated (exit code 0, reason Completed) after SIGTERM; liveness probe continues failing with 404.", "citations": ["ev_a1dac7f4b2", "ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}], "root_cause": {"status": "identified", "category": "probe_misconfig", "object": {"kind": "Deployment", "namespace": "demo-s1", "name": "s1-app", "field": "spec.template.spec.containers[app].livenessProbe.httpGet.path"}, "statement": "The liveness probe path was changed from /healthz to /status, but the application does not serve /status, so the probe returns HTTP 404 and Kubernetes repeatedly kills and restarts the container.", "citations": ["ev_f88a94b86c", "ev_42c4b2ed46", "ev_5f9afc980a", "ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"], "confidence": "high"}, "claims": [{"statement": "The liveness probe HTTP GET /status returns HTTP 404, causing the container to be killed and restarted.", "citations": ["ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}, {"statement": "The readiness probe still targets /healthz and fails with connection refused/reset, indicating the container is not ready.", "citations": ["ev_5f9afc980a", "ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}, {"statement": "The application starts cleanly: it allocates 48 MiB, listens on port 8080, and exits with code 0 on SIGTERM, with no error output in the logs.", "citations": ["ev_80b93df6c5", "ev_32a0d35da1", "ev_a1dac7f4b2"]}, {"statement": "The container is terminated externally (SIGTERM) rather than crashing from an internal error.", "citations": ["ev_80b93df6c5", "ev_32a0d35da1", "ev_a1dac7f4b2"]}, {"statement": "The only change between revision 1 and revision 2 of the Deployment is the liveness probe path (/healthz to /status).", "citations": ["ev_42c4b2ed46", "ev_f88a94b86c"]}, {"statement": "No image pull errors occurred; the image bianque-s1-app:dev was already present on the node.", "citations": ["ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}, {"statement": "The pod s1-app-7fb788b78f-7xq95 belongs to ReplicaSet s1-app-7fb788b78f (revision 2).", "citations": ["ev_a1dac7f4b2", "ev_42c4b2ed46"]}], "missing_evidence": [{"what": "The application's served HTTP endpoints (to confirm /status is not implemented and /healthz is the correct liveness endpoint).", "reason": "No application source code or endpoint listing was available in the evidence; the 404 on /status and the clean startup logs are the only indicators."}], "suggestions": [{"action": "Revert the liveness probe path from /status back to /healthz (or point it at an endpoint the application actually serves) in deployment.yaml and re-apply.", "risk": "change", "command": "kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml", "citations": ["ev_f88a94b86c", "ev_42c4b2ed46", "ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}, {"action": "Confirm which HTTP endpoint the application exposes for liveness before changing the probe path.", "risk": "read_only", "citations": ["ev_6c30168c89", "ev_82a2fba83b"]}], "references": [{"knowledge_id": "kn_b728d580f575", "title": "CrashLoopBackOff > What CrashLoopBackOff means"}, {"knowledge_id": "kn_c73d8439117f", "title": "CrashLoopBackOff > Reading the previous container log"}, {"knowledge_id": "kn_fa369be3768e", "title": "CrashLoopBackOff > Collecting the termination state"}, {"knowledge_id": "kn_255795fa4d69", "title": "CrashLoopBackOff > Restart backoff timing"}], "followup_questions": ["Does the s1-app application actually implement a /status endpoint, or is /healthz the only health endpoint?", "Why was the liveness probe moved to /status without a corresponding application change?", "Should the readiness probe also be reviewed, given it is failing with connection refused/reset?"]}
